Phần cần sửa là cách vận dụng khung: “Admittedly, one might argue” mượn lời khi em chỉ thừa nhận một lợi ích có thật, khiến câu dài mà không rõ phe đối lập; “This may evoke emotions” chưa gọi rõ trải nghiệm trực tiếp; ví dụ sau đó chỉ nói xem chi tiết mà chưa cho thấy cảm xúc/tính chân thực. paragraphs: Nowadays, some people argue that public museums and art galleries may become unnecessary as people can view historical objects and works of art on a computer. Personally, I am of the opposite school of thought.

Admittedly, technology brings significant benefits to people seeking cultural and historical resources. High-resolution images, three-dimensional reconstructions; virtual reality platforms enable viewers to explore masterpieces and ancient artefacts in remarkable detail without leaving home. For instance, the Louvre museum provides many items from its collection on online platforms, allowing people who cannot afford to travel or have mobility issues to still access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

However, I strongly believe that public museums and art galleries are still essential. Initially, the online experience cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing an artefact or artwork in person. Seeing such objects in person may evoke emotions and a sense of authenticity that digital images cannot convey. For example, visitors can see historical objects and artworks in galleries up close, appreciate their details and feel more connected to the past. Furthermore, museums and galleries are vital cultural hubs that symbolize the identity of a region. This cultural role can attract tourists and foster bonding within the community.
In conclusion, in light of these arguments, I strongly challenge the perspective that public museums and art galleries will become unnecessary.

paragraphs: Nowadays, some people argue that public museums and art galleries may become unnecessary because they can access historical objects and works of art through their computer. Personally, I am of the opposite school of thought.

Admittedly, one might argue that technology brings significant benefits to accessing cultural and historical resources. High-resolution images, three-dimensional reconstructions; virtual reality platforms enable viewers to explore masterpieces and ancient artefacts in remarkable detail without leaving home. For instance, the Louvre museum provides many of its collection on online platforms, allowing people who cannot afford and have mobility issues to still access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

However, I strongly believe that public museums and art galleries are still essential. Initially, the online experience cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing an artefact or artwork in person. This may evoke emotions and a sense of authenticity that digital images cannot convey. For example, visitors can see historical objects and artworks in galleries, allowing them to appreciate details and understand their true meaning. Furthermore, museums and galleries are vital cultural hubs that symbolize the identity of a region. This become a magnet for tourism and a facilitator of bonding within the community.
In conclusion, in the light of the aforementioned arguments, I strongly challenge perspective that public museums become unnecessary.

task.text:
Some people claim that public museums and art galleries will be no longer needed because people can see historical objects and works of art by using a computer.
To what extent do you agree or disagree?
